Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
727 AM EDT Sun Oct 11 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 251 AM EDT Sunday...

Tonight is trending drier for northern areas.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 251 AM EDT Sunday...

1. Rain associated with the remnants of Isaias will bring a 
some rainfall tonight with no significant impacts for our area. 

2. Periods of rain Tuesday into Tuesday night before drying on 
Wednesday. 

3. Low pressure system brings next chance for showers Friday 
into Friday night with showers continuing into the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 251 AM EDT Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: The center of the low associated with the 
remnants of Isaias will track up into the Mid-Atlantic then 
track offshore before it reaches any farther north. Rainfall 
will spread into southern areas this evening but struggle to 
make it any farther north as it is running into the ~1030 MB 
high that is giving us the dry weekend. The 00Z guidance has 
trended south with the northern extent of the rain, with the 
global deterministic data showing the most dramatic retreat 
while the HREF and global ensembles show a more subtle retreat. 
Overall, areas with a 50 percent or higher chance of seeing 0.1 
inches is now mostly restricted to southern Vermont, with 
measurable rain likely not reaching the international border in 
places. Forecast rain amounts range from close to a half inch in
southern Windsor/Rutland counties to nothing along much of 
Quebec border.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A surface low will pass through from west to 
east Tuesday night, bringing widespread showers. While it will 
be quick moving and technically more northern stream and not 
have a strong connection to Gulf/Atlantic moisture, it will 
include the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachael so there will be 
some efficient rainfall with the former tropical moisture. 
GEFS/EPS/CMCE combined probabilities of a half inch of rain 
range between 40-70 percent and probabilities of an inch are 
between 10-30 percent, so the rain would only be beneficial. The
heaviest rain should fall in northern areas. Warm air aloft 
will remain on the backside so even though the cold front drops 
temperatures significantly, any upslope showers look to remain 
rain in the mountains. Conditions trend drier for Wednesday, but
under a classic cyclonic northwest flow cold air advection 
regime, there will be some upslope sprinkles and showers but no 
widespread rain.

KEY MESSAGE 3: A dynamic low pressure system brings winds and 
rain to the region for Friday into Saturday. Showers will linger
behind this system as upper level trough remains over the 
region. Still a lot of uncertainty about this system since it is
six days away. Models are still not in very good agreement in 
this timeframe either. GFS has a deeper and stronger low while 
the ECMWF depicts more of an open wave as the system moves 
through.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Through 12Z Monday...VFR conditions are expected through 00Z 
Monday. Winds will increase from the south today, especially in 
the Champlain Valley. Some afternoon gusts 15-25 knots are 
expected at KBTV and KPBG. EFK and MSS should remain dry through
the 24 hour TAF period. Other sites have some mention of -RA. 
Best chances for precipitation will be at RUT and MPV. It's 
possible those will be the only 2 sites with rain. Ceilings will
lower as precipitation moves in, down to MVFR in some 
instances. 

Outlook...

Columbus Day: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Monday Night: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Likely SHRA.
Tuesday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Definite SHRA.
Tuesday Night: MVFR. Definite SHRA.
Wednesday: Mainly MVFR, with local VFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Wednesday Night: MVFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Thursday: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.

&&

.MARINE...
As of 251 AM EDT Sunday...Southerly winds will continue to 
increase as the night goes on and sustained winds in the 20-30 
KT range should prevail for much of the day. Waves will trend 
upward as well, reaching the 2-3 ft range in much of the broad 
lake. Some isolated instances of 4 ft waves are possible. Winds 
and waves will gradually come down tonight, with winds dropping 
to around and under 10 KT by tomorrow morning and decreasing to 
around and below a foot by then.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$
